content:
About a week ago I was faced with some crazy FLT slowdowns when bumping to v4.29, which I believe have the same underlying source as the slowdowns in mathlib created in #34049 and flagged here #rss > Significant commits to mathlib4 @ 💬 . The slowdowns are caused by making WithVal a one-field structure (which I think is a good idea).

I spent several days trying to debug what was actually going on in FLT, resulting in the thread #mathlib4 > instance unfolding phenomenon . During this time I also asked @Jovan Gerbscheid for a clear description of what fast_instance% does, which he kindly gave me.

I believe there are two independent things going on: (1) typeclass inference unfolding more than it should (Riccardo's beautiful #mwe demonstrating the problem is here #mathlib4 > instance unfolding phenomenon @ 💬 and Jovan's explanation is here #mathlib4 > instance unfolding phenomenon @ 💬 ) and (2) the unfolding suddenly costing a lot more than it used to (because WithVal is now a one-field structure so things are being pulled across Equivs which adds even more friction). On one of my devices I was hacking the copy of mathlib in FLT throwing around fast_instance% randomly, trying to tame the problem, and once I got the FLT bump to v4.29 over the line (with a bunch of slowdowns and backwards transparency technical debt :-/ ) I remembered the hacks and just tried them on master in #38087 . It results in a 215.2G speed-up in instructions, more than cancelling out the slowdown caused by #34049 . I simply don't know whether the speed-up is caused by less unfolding happening or unfolding being cheaper -- both phenomena might contribute to speedups and fast_instance% might play a role in both.

My question is this: if a random scattergun fast_instance% approach can give such a speed-up, (a) which of those instances is actually doing the work and which are irrelevant in #38087 and (b) where else can we put fast_instance% in mathlib and make big speedups? I am not claiming, at all, that I know what I am doing here, but there are some wins to be had and it would be nice to understand things better and perhaps find more wins.
There are still some leaky instances for WithVal that need to be solved with fast_instance%. I was also looking at these. My guess is that the speedup you are seeing comes from doing this.

Yes, looking at some traces I think you're right. It seems to be lots of very small speed-ups coming from these random Int.cast = Int.cast, Neg = Neg etc etc goals all now being slightly quicker to solve.
